kicker: A statistical model of professional hockey
title: The Read the Ice Model
body: On what it measures, how it is tested, and what it does not claim.

title: A goal is an outcome. It is not a measurement.
body: Over short spans, the score of a hockey game is governed largely by variance.
The model therefore sets results aside and measures the process that produces them: the quantity and the quality of the scoring chances each player and each team creates and allows.
Two complete seasons of play. Each shot is assigned a probability of becoming a goal, estimated from its location, the sequence of events that preceded it, and the speed at which the play developed.

title: Recomputed in full, twice daily.
body: The model is re-estimated from the complete record after each night's final game, and again once lineups and starting goaltenders are confirmed.
Every rate is shrunk toward prior evidence in proportion to its uncertainty, so that a small sample is never mistaken for a signal.

title: Stated probability against observed frequency.
after: 894 goals expected; 913 observed, across 5,747 player-games. Each estimate was archived before the opening faceoff and graded afterward. Before release, the model was tested out of sample on 1,241 games.
note: Goal probabilities, Oct 16 to Nov 8, 2026 · For information and entertainment. 21+.

title: What the model does not claim.
body: It does not predict the outcome of any single game. It does not offer certainty.
It reports a probability, the evidence behind it, and its own record. Nothing more is asserted.
